versions.label: Vulnerable
versions.summary: The preview endpoint checks the host of the URL it was given once, then fetches it with a client that follows redirects on its own.
versions.outcome: The preview endpoint returned the internal service's marker, reached through a redirect on an allowed host.

sinkline.out:
[HIGH] SL-SSRF-001 A10:2021 CWE-918  app.py:23:24
  SSRF: tainted URL fetched server-side
  flask.request.args reaches requests.get without a sanitizer for CWE-918.
  ┌ source     app.py:19  url = request.args.get("url", "")  # flask.request.args
  │ propagate  app.py:19  url = request.args.get("url", "")  # .get()
  └ sink       app.py:23  upstream = requests.get(url, timeout=3)  # requests.get
  fix: Allow-list hosts/schemes, resolve DNS and reject private ranges, disable redirects.

1 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 6 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery: 1

versions.label: Fixed
versions.summary: The app follows redirects itself, at most three hops, and checks every hop's host and resolved address before connecting to that address.
versions.outcome: Both the direct and the redirected request were refused and the internal service was never contacted.

sinkline.out:
[HIGH] SL-SSRF-001 A10:2021 CWE-918  app.py:42:24
  SSRF: tainted URL fetched server-side
  flask.request.args reaches requests.get (inside fetch, app.py:33) without a sanitizer for CWE-918.
  ┌ source     app.py:42  upstream = fetch(request.args.get("url", ""))  # flask.request.args
  │ propagate  app.py:42  upstream = fetch(request.args.get("url", ""))  # .get()
  │ call       app.py:42  upstream = fetch(request.args.get("url", ""))  # passed as `url` to fetch()
  └ sink       app.py:33  upstream = requests.get(pinned, headers={"Host": host_header}, allow_redirects=False, timeout=3)  # requests.get inside fetch()
  fix: Allow-list hosts/schemes, resolve DNS and reject private ranges, disable redirects.

1 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 8 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery: 1
sinkline.note: False positive. sinkline does not recognize a custom allow-list or address pinning as a sanitizer.

versions.label: Vulnerable
versions.summary: The search text is bound as a query parameter, but the sort column is pasted into the SQL string.
versions.outcome: A sort value made a second table decide the order of the rows that came back.

sinkline.out:
[CRITICAL] SL-SQLI-001 A03:2021 CWE-89  app.py:19:24
  SQL built from tainted data
  flask.request.args reaches sqlite3.Connection.execute without a sanitizer for CWE-89.
  ┌ source     app.py:13  sort = request.args.get("sort", "name")  # flask.request.args
  │ propagate  app.py:13  sort = request.args.get("sort", "name")  # .get()
  │ propagate  app.py:16  query = f"SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE ? ORDER BY {sort} {direction}"  # f-string
  └ sink       app.py:19  rows = conn.execute(query, (needle,)).fetchall()  # sqlite3.Connection.execute
  fix: Use parameterized queries: conn.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))

1 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 4 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: A03:2021 Injection: 1

versions.label: Fixed
versions.summary: The sort value is looked up in a dictionary of columns the application owns; anything else is a 400.
versions.outcome: The same sort values got a 400 and nothing from the second table appeared in a response.

sinkline.out:
[CRITICAL] SL-SQLI-001 A03:2021 CWE-89  app.py:22:20
  SQL built from tainted data
  flask.request.args reaches sqlite3.Connection.execute without a sanitizer for CWE-89.
  ┌ source     app.py:15  column = SORT_COLUMNS.get(request.args.get("sort", "name"))  # flask.request.args
  │ propagate  app.py:15  column = SORT_COLUMNS.get(request.args.get("sort", "name"))  # .get()
  │ call       app.py:15  column = SORT_COLUMNS.get(request.args.get("sort", "name"))  # SORT_COLUMNS.get() (unknown; assumed passthrough)
  │ propagate  app.py:15  column = SORT_COLUMNS.get(request.args.get("sort", "name"))  # assigned to `column`
  │ propagate  app.py:20  query = f"SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE ? ORDER BY {column} {direction}"  # f-string
  └ sink       app.py:22  rows = conn.execute(query, (needle,)).fetchall()  # sqlite3.Connection.execute
  fix: Use parameterized queries: conn.execute('... WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))

1 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 4 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: A03:2021 Injection: 1
sinkline.note: False positive. sinkline treats the allow-list dictionary lookup as an unknown call and assumes passthrough.

versions.label: Vulnerable
versions.summary: The read-by-id route checks that someone is logged in but not that the invoice is theirs; the list and update routes do check.
versions.outcome: A logged-in user received another user's invoice, including its memo, and every one of the eight ids answered 200.

sinkline.out:
0 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 12 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: none
sinkline.note: Not reported, as the write-up expects: a missing authorization check is not a taint flow.

versions.label: Fixed
versions.summary: One helper checks ownership and every by-id route goes through it; a record that is not yours answers 404.
versions.outcome: Every record the user did not own answered 404 on read and on update, and the other user's memo never appeared.

sinkline.out:
0 finding(s) in 1 file(s), 16 function(s) summarized
by OWASP: none

titles: One session reads many different invoice ids in a short time
